Nucleus Net

Teach a tiny neural network to call nuclear irregularity — and watch every node and weight while it learns.

One hundred nuclei, one question: is the contour regular?

These are synthetic nuclei, drawn by a script so that we know the truth for every one. Half have a smooth, elliptical membrane; half are irregular — lobulated, notched or finely jagged. Everything else that could give the game away — size, elongation, rotation, hyperchromasia, chromatin texture, a nucleolus, position in the crop — is drawn from the same distribution in both groups. The only honest way to score well is to look at the outline.

Eighty nuclei form the training set, which the network learns from. Twenty are held out as a test set: the network never sees them during training, so they tell us whether it learned something general or merely memorised the eighty.

Click any nucleus to put it under the inspector on the right. There you can see the six measurements a morphometry pipeline would make on it — the same six the network can be given as its input in stage 2.

    Nucleus Net is a teaching toy: a fully connected network with hand-written backpropagation, trained in your browser on 100 synthetic nuclei. Keys: 1 2 3 switch stages, space trains or pauses, N classifies the next test nucleus. Regenerate the specimens with node tools/generate_nuclei.js.
